paragraphs.paragraph: The psalm presents David in the wilderness of Judah, amid deprivation, loneliness, and danger, and shows how these conditions intensify his thirst for God and his longing to see His power and glory.
paragraphs.title: Longing for God in the Wilderness

answers: In a dry and thirsty land
easy.explanation: David describes being in a dry and thirsty land where no water is.
easy.q: Where does David say he is at the beginning of the psalm?

easy.explanation: David directly addresses God as his God.
easy.q: To whom does David say, “O God, thou art my God”?

easy.explanation: David says, “my soul thirsteth for thee.”
easy.q: What does David’s soul thirst for?

answers: It intensifies his longing for God
It causes him to forget God
It makes him gladly abandon his faith
medium.explanation: The dry and difficult setting highlights David’s deep spiritual thirst for God.
medium.q: How does the wilderness setting affect David?

medium.explanation: David says he longs “to see thy power and thy glory.”
medium.q: What does David desire to see in the sanctuary?

medium.explanation: The phrase explicitly describes a dry land lacking water.
medium.q: What does “a dry and thirsty land, where no water is” describe?

answers: Physical thirst is unrelated to David’s soul
The wilderness thirst expresses and intensifies his longing for God
Thirst causes David to think only about water
challenge.explanation: The lack of water provides the setting for David’s deeper thirst for God.
challenge.q: How does the psalm connect physical thirst with spiritual longing?

answers: From wilderness deprivation to longing to see God’s glory
From praise to enemies and then to the king
challenge.explanation: The verses move from the dry wilderness to David’s desire for God’s power and glory.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in these verses?

answers: Thirst, seeking God, and seeing His glory
challenge.explanation: David thirsts for God, seeks Him early, and longs to see His power and glory.
challenge.q: Which three ideas are joined in David’s longing?

paragraphs.idea: The psalm presents David in the wilderness of Judah, amid deprivation, loneliness, and danger, and shows how these conditions intensify his thirst for God and his longing to see His power and glory.

paragraphs.paragraph: David places God’s loving-kindness above life itself and responds with blessing, prayer, raised hands, and praise that give him inner fullness and refreshment.
paragraphs.title: Kindness, Prayer, and Praise

easy.explanation: David declares, “thy lovingkindness is better than life.”
easy.q: How does David compare God’s loving-kindness with life?

easy.explanation: David says, “I will lift up my hands in thy name.”
easy.q: What does David lift up in God’s name?

easy.explanation: David says, “my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.”

answers: With blessing, lifted hands, and praise
medium.explanation: David blesses God, lifts his hands, and praises Him.
medium.q: How does David respond to God’s loving-kindness?

medium.explanation: David says his soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness.
medium.q: What does the image of “marrow and fatness” represent?

answers: His praise expresses the fullness of his soul
His praise prevents him from praying
His praise describes his lack of water
medium.explanation: After describing his satisfied soul, David speaks of praising God with joyful lips.
medium.q: What is the relationship between David’s satisfaction and his praise?

answers: That life has no value at all
That God’s loving-kindness is his highest value
That David wants to withdraw from God
challenge.explanation: David places God’s loving-kindness above life itself.
challenge.q: What does saying that God’s loving-kindness is better than life reveal about David’s priorities?

answers: Raised hands and praise express the soul’s satisfaction
The inward feeling has no outward response
challenge.explanation: David’s inner satisfaction is expressed through blessing, lifted hands, and joyful praise.
challenge.q: How do outward actions and inward feelings work together in these verses?

answers: God’s loving-kindness, blessing and prayer, then satisfaction and praise
Enemies, the sword, and then the wilderness
challenge.explanation: David first speaks of God’s loving-kindness, then responds with worship and describes spiritual satisfaction.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: David places God’s loving-kindness above life itself and responds with blessing, prayer, raised hands, and praise that give him inner fullness and refreshment.

paragraphs.paragraph: Even at night David remembers and meditates on God, feels sheltered under His protection, and clings to Him, knowing that His right hand supports him.
paragraphs.title: God’s Presence and Support

easy.explanation: David remembers God upon his bed and meditates in the night watches.
easy.q: When does David remember and meditate on God?

easy.explanation: David says, “in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.”
easy.q: In whose shadow does David rejoice?

easy.explanation: David says, “My soul followeth hard after thee.”
easy.q: What does David’s soul do toward God?

medium.explanation: David rejoices in the shadow of God’s wings, a picture of divine protection.
medium.q: What gives David a sense of protection?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the watches or periods of the night.
medium.q: What does “the night watches” refer to?

answers: God’s support makes David turn away
medium.explanation: David connects following hard after God with the knowledge that God’s right hand upholds him.
medium.q: How is God’s right hand related to David’s devotion?

answers: Remembering and meditating, finding protection, following and being upheld
challenge.explanation: The verses move from nighttime remembrance to shelter, devotion, and divine support.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes David’s growing relationship with God?

challenge.explanation: The image portrays David resting securely under God’s protection.
challenge.q: What does the image of “the shadow of thy wings” communicate?

answers: As a time when David forgets God
As a time of remembrance, meditation, and rejoicing
As a time devoted only to warfare
challenge.explanation: At night David remembers and meditates on God and rejoices in His shelter.
challenge.q: How does the psalm portray the nighttime?

paragraphs.idea: Even at night David remembers and meditates on God, feels sheltered under His protection, and clings to Him, knowing that His right hand supports him.

paragraphs.paragraph: The psalmist turns to enemies who seek his life and expresses a wish for their downfall, then describes the king rejoicing in God and the silencing of those who speak lies.
paragraphs.title: Enemies, the King, and the Liars

easy.explanation: The enemies are described as those that seek David’s soul to destroy it.
The verse says, “the king shall rejoice in God.”
easy.q: In whom shall the king rejoice?

answers: It will be heard far away
easy.explanation: The psalm concludes that the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.
easy.q: What will happen to the mouth of those who speak lies?

medium.explanation: The passage describes their destruction and descent into the lower parts of the earth.
medium.q: What does David express concerning those who seek his soul?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that their lying speech will be silenced.
medium.q: What does it mean that the mouth of liars “shall be stopped”?

answers: Enemies are described, the king rejoices, and liars are silenced
The wilderness is described, prayer is offered, and David sleeps
Loving-kindness is praised, thirst is described, and hands are lifted
medium.explanation: The verses move from enemies to the king’s rejoicing and finally to the stopping of lying mouths.
medium.q: What is the order of ideas in the final verses?

answers: The king rejoicing in God versus enemies and liars
challenge.explanation: The king is pictured rejoicing in God, while enemies fall and liars are silenced.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears at the end of the psalm?

answers: The enemies and liars are not shown as victorious
The liars are honored and praised
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the enemies’ downfall and the silencing of false speech.
challenge.q: How does the description of the enemies relate to the psalm’s theme of justice?

answers: The psalm moves from threat to security and joy in God
The psalm moves from joy to fear only
The psalm stops speaking about God
challenge.explanation: After describing danger from enemies, the psalm turns to the king’s joy in God.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the movement from enemies to the king?

paragraphs.idea: The psalmist turns to enemies who seek his life and expresses a wish for their downfall, then describes the king rejoicing in God and the silencing of those who speak lies.
